title: Ten Thousand Talents Once I Owed
description: Ten Thousand Talents Once I Owed in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 67, “The happy debtor”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ten thou-sand tal-ents once I owed, And noth-ing had to pay; But Je-sus freed me from the load, And washed my debt a-way.

lines: Ten thousand talents once I owed,
But Jesus freed me from the load,
Yet since the Lord forgave my sin,
Much more indebted I have been,
My guilt is cancelled quite, I know,
But the vast debt of love I owe,
The love I owe for sin forgiv'n,
For present peace, and promised heav'n,
That love of thine! thou sinner's Friend!
My little all can ne'er extend
Nay more, the poor returns I make
And 'tis of grace, that thou wilt take
To owe thee more and more.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
